themes.name: Agents Break Web Assumptions
themes.plain: Software agents now browse, buy, and act for people, but the systems underneath were built for humans clicking pages. Several of the hardest problems exist because the stack cannot tell who or what is on the other end, or what it is allowed to do.
themes.evidence: The problems on distinguishing and governing agentic traffic and on safe, auditable agent execution both sit near the top of the board, and the answers reach for new agent-only endpoints, delegation tokens, and write gateways because the human web offers none.

themes.name: Machines Cannot Judge Meaning
themes.plain: The hardest checks depend on context and implied meaning, and software cannot reliably do that. So the models retreat to a narrower move: limit what the system is allowed to say or do, rather than try to judge each case.
themes.evidence: On governing generative marketing content at volume, all three models say claim substantiation and brand risk turn on context that tools cannot interpret, and all three fall back to locking down a library of pre-approved claims and constraining what the model may write.

themes.name: Start From What Already Failed
themes.plain: Every model opens the same way: go find the cases you already have answers for and turn them into training data or rules. Nobody starts by designing the ideal system.
themes.evidence: On generative content governance all three begin by mining recent legal rejections to learn what reviewers actually caught, and on agentic traffic the first moves are labeling sessions already known to be agents and measuring in shadow mode before changing anything.

themes.name: Chokepoint Before Trust
themes.plain: When the models cannot trust what is acting, they route everything through one door they own. Put a proxy or gateway in front of every write, log it, cap it, and keep a kill switch, because a sent message or a spent budget cannot be taken back.
themes.evidence: On safe, auditable agent execution all three answers propose a single proxy or gateway with hard limits on rate, budget, and audience size, and all three name irreversible third-party effects with no rollback as the core difficulty.

themes.name: Governance At Machine Speed
themes.plain: Content, consent, and actions are now produced faster than any human can review them. Much of the board is about proving control after the fact instead of approving each item in advance.
themes.evidence: The problem of governing generative marketing content at volume, together with provable downstream consent and deletion enforcement, keeps the answers focused on audit trails, locked libraries, and logged limits rather than case-by-case human sign-off.
